content:
Geometry in Class 3 covers shapes, faces/edges/vertices, lines and angles, symmetry and perimeter — visual, high-scoring Olympiad content. Here is what the IMO Class 3 geometry chapter tests, the facts to know, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 3 Maths Olympiad Geometry chapter tests

  • 2-D shapes (sides, corners) and 3-D shapes (faces, edges, vertices)
  • Points, lines, rays and line segments; angles
  • Symmetry
  • Perimeter

Key facts your child should know

  • A cube and a cuboid each have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
  • A cylinder has 3 faces, 2 edges, 0 vertices; a cone has 2 faces, 1 edge, 1 vertex; a sphere has 1 curved face.
  • A line segment has two endpoints; a ray goes on one way; a line goes on both ways.
  • Perimeter is the distance around a shape — add every side (a square of side 5 cm has perimeter 20 cm).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing up edges and vertices on a solid.
  • Confusing a ray, a line and a line segment.
  • Adding only two sides for the perimeter of a rectangle.

quiz.title: IMO Class 3 Geometry Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: How many corners are shared when two squares are joined along one full side?
questions.explanation: The two squares share the two corners at the ends of the joined side.

questions.q: The edge of a ruler is an example of a
questions.explanation: A ruler’s edge is perfectly straight — a straight line.

questions.q: Which two solids have NO vertices at all?
questions.explanation: A sphere and a cylinder have no corners (vertices); a cone has one.

questions.q: A brick is most like which solid?
questions.explanation: A brick has 6 rectangular faces, so it is a cuboid.

questions.q: The largest face of a matchbox (cuboid) is dipped in ink and pressed on paper. The print is a
questions.explanation: The faces of a cuboid are rectangles, so the print is a rectangle.

questions.q: How many more vertices than faces does a cuboid have?
questions.explanation: A cuboid has 8 vertices and 6 faces: 8 − 6 = 2 more.

questions.q: What is the total number of faces, edges and vertices of a cube?
A line that is neither exactly horizontal nor vertical, but tilted, is called a
questions.explanation: A tilted line is a slanting (oblique) line.

questions.q: I am a solid with no flat face and no edge; I am curved all over. Who am I?
questions.explanation: Only a sphere is curved everywhere with no flat face and no edge.

questions.q: How many more edges does a cube have than a cone?
questions.explanation: Cube has 12 edges, cone has 1 edge: 12 - 1 = 11.

faq.q: How do you find the perimeter of a shape?
faq.a: Add the lengths of all its sides. For a rectangle it is 2 × (length + breadth).

faq.q: How many edges does a cube have?
faq.a: Twelve, along with 6 faces and 8 vertices.
